harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Published node1’s approved release tree as the persistent, read-only rsync module `releases`. Node2 retrieved it with file modes, ownership, content, and symlink intact. Uploads, private-module access, and path traversal are denied. Both nodes were restarted sequentially and fully recovered with changed boot identities.
actions_performed: Configured node1’s native rsync 2.6.9 SysV daemon without changing the legacy OS or kernel.
Restricted the module root to `/srv/legacy2/rsync-module-publication/releases`, enabled chroot/read-only operation, and limited access to node2.
Retrieved the complete release tree on node2 using archive mode.
Verified matching manifests and hashes, preserved `current -> v1`, upload rejection, and denial of access outside the module.
Restarted node1 and node2 one at a time and verified persistence and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Persistent read-only rsync daemon module named releases
evidence.summary: Shows the enabled daemon, listening service, effective chroot/read-only configuration, and successful access after both restarts.

evidence.requirement: Node2 retrieves the full tree with file modes and symlinks intact
evidence.summary: Source and retrieved manifests match, including modes, ownership, hashes, and `current -> v1`; post-restart retrieval returns success.

evidence.requirement: Writes and access outside the release tree are denied
evidence.summary: Upload attempts receive `module is read only`; `private` is not exported; traversal fails and creates no escaped file, including after restarts.

evidence.requirement: Approved release, private data, OS release, and kernel are preserved
evidence.summary: Initial and final release/private hashes and metadata match; the legacy 2.6.22 kernel and installed rsync 2.6.9 remain in use.
Captures healthy baseline boot ID, reboot acknowledgment, changed boot ID, recovered daemon/listener and data, and a successful client read.
Captures healthy baseline boot ID and retrieved data, reboot acknowledgment, changed boot ID, successful post-restart retrieval, preserved metadata/hashes, and security checks.
